ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
<image>In $\odot G, m \angle A G B=30$ and $\overline{C G} \perp \overline{G D}$.
Find $m \widehat{B C}$
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Geometry3K open-ended question

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a circle with G as the center, and A, B, C, D are all on the circle. Segment A-G-D looks like a straight line passing through the center of the circle, so AD is a diameter, and GA and GD are opposite rays. Rays GA, GB, GC, GD are distributed in order in the direction of the upper semicircle. The figure also marks a right-angle mark that CG is perpendicular to GD. Reasoning: It is given that m∠AGB = 30. Because CG ⟂ GD, m∠CGD = 90. Since GA and GD are opposite rays, ∠AGD is a straight angle, with measure 180°. ∠AGB, ∠BGC, ∠CGD together form this straight angle, therefore m∠BGC = 180 - 30 - 90 = 60. Arc BC is intercepted by central angle ∠BGC, so m arc BC = 60.

Since GA and GD are opposite rays, the central angles ∠AGB, ∠BGC, and ∠CGD partition the straight angle ∠AGD = 180. Thus m∠BGC = 180 - 30 - 90 = 60. Because arc BC is intercepted by central angle ∠BGC, m arc BC = 60.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram by assigning directions from the center G: GD points to the right, GA is the opposite ray on the same diameter, and GC is perpendicular to GD, pointing upward toward point C. Therefore ∠AGC is the angle between the ray opposite GD and the ray perpendicular to GD, so m∠AGC = 90. The text gives m∠AGB = 30, and the image shows ray GB lies between GA and GC. Therefore m∠BGC = m∠AGC - m∠AGB = 90 - 30 = 60. Since ∠BGC is the central angle that subtends arc BC, m arc BC = 60.
